item.research_question: Can friction stir processing (FSP) enhance the strength and ductility of a dual-phase high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a composition of Fe50Mn30Co10Cr10 (at.%)?
item.processing_route: Friction stir processing (FSP) with tool rotational rates of 350 and 650 RPM
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 10−3 s−1
key_findings: The FSP-engineered microstructure exhibited a substantially smaller grain size, with average grain sizes of 6.5 and 5.2 µm, respectively.
The FSP treatment led to a significantly higher fraction of f.c.c. γ-phase in the microstructure of the TRIP HEA.
The FSP specimens showed enhanced strength and ductility, with maximum true stress values of 1400 MPa and 1200 MPa at uniform elongations of almost 45% and 42%, respectively.
The TRIP effect was enhanced in the FSP specimens, with a higher level of TRIP-related strain hardening during deformation.
The strength-ductility index (SDI) values of the FSP specimens were higher than those of the as-homogenized reference material.
The FSP-engineered DP-HEA showed a similar f.c.c. γ average grain size as compared to the TMP-HEA reported by Li et al., but with a lower h.c.p. ε-phase fraction.
The difference in the SDI values for the 350 and 650 RPM treated specimens could be explained by considering both the grain refinement and the ε-phase fraction prior to tensile deformation.
item.mechanism: The enhanced strength and ductility of the FSP-engineered HEA were attributed to the synergistic effects of grain boundary strengthening, TRIP, and effective strain partitioning between the γ and ε phases during deformation.
item.limitations: The study only investigated the effects of FSP on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the HEA, without exploring other processing techniques or conditions.
item.future_work: Further studies are needed to optimize the processing conditions and explore the potential of FSP for other HEA compositions.
quotes: Friction stir processing resulted in a fine grain size along with a high volume fraction of f.c.c. (γ) phase as compared to as-homogenized reference material.
The TRIP HEAs exhibit very high values of the strength-ductility product index and the response can be tailored through microstructural engineering.
The initial FSP results also provide a first overview of the alloy’s suitability for joining via friction stir welding.
